source_caption:
To completely capture the wildly kinetic, breathlessly exhilarating energy of the iconic “Trolley Song” musical number, director Vincente Minnelli made an incredibly daring technical gamble. Instead of filming the scene with standard, heavily edited static shots, Minnelli ordered the massive MGM crew to lay down hundreds of feet of dolly tracks exactly parallel to the physical trolley car set. He then filmed Judy Garland belting the famously fast-paced lyrics in one profoundly complex, massive tracking shot as the camera aggressively kept pace alongside the moving trolley. By refusing to chop up the sequence in the editing room, Minnelli masterfully proves that the most deeply infectious cinematic joy is achieved by simply locking the camera onto a wildly brilliant star and letting her completely soar.
⠀
Meet Me in St. Louis (1944), directed by Vincente Minnelli, starring Judy Garland, Margaret O’Brien, Mary Astor. A fiercely close-knit, deeply traditional Missouri family experiences a wildly emotional, beautifully poignant year of romance and heartbreak as they frantically prepare to completely uproot their happy lives and move to New York City right before the massive 1904 World’s Fair.

source_details.synopsis: Meet Me in St. Louis is a 1944 American musical film in Technicolor made by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. Divided into a series of seasonal vignettes, starting with Summer 1903, it relates the story of a year in the life of the Smith family in St. Louis leading up to the opening of the Louisiana Purchase Exposition (most commonly referred to as the World's Fair) in the spring of 1904. The film stars Judy Garland, Margaret O'Brien, Mary Astor, Lucille Bremer, Tom Drake, Leon Ames, Marjorie Main, Harry Davenport, June Lockhart, and Joan Carroll.
